p.title: v59.97 a model FOMC headline in English could be stored and block every later release at preflight
p.symptom: ci-headline-translation-check (blocking preflight) requires every event-briefs.json headline to hold at least two Hangul syllables, but the producer stored the FOMC model headline whenever its numbers verified (English included) and briefHeadline accepted a single Hangul character. An English FOMC headline would fail every release's preflight for the up-to-10 days the brief stays in the file.
p.root_cause: The producer and the gate applied different rules: safeHeadline checked only numbers, briefHeadline tested /[가-힣]/ (one syllable), while the gate requires two syllables.
p.fix: One exported rule isKoreanHeadline (>= 2 Hangul syllables) in src/domain/briefing/event-briefs.js, used by briefHeadline and by the producer's safeHeadline; a non-Korean model headline falls back to the producer's own line (FOMC: 'M/D FOMC 결정'; earnings: '<name> 실적: <figure>' or '<name> 실적 발표').
p.violated_rule: A producer owns the rule its blocking gate checks: an artifact the gate would reject is never written.
p.prevention: ci-event-briefs-check v59.97 cases drive buildEventBriefs with an English, a one-syllable and a Korean FOMC model headline, and briefHeadline with a one-syllable headline.
p.verification: node scripts/ci-event-briefs-check.mjs (the FOMC English and one-syllable cases fail on the old producer, the briefHeadline case on the old source; all pass now); node scripts/ci-headline-translation-check.mjs exit 0.

changelog: **Brief headlines follow the preflight rule ({P}):** the event-brief producer now stores a model headline only when it holds at least two Hangul syllables (the headline-translation gate's rule); an English or one-syllable FOMC or earnings headline is replaced by the producer's own Korean line, so a model answer can no longer freeze releases.
note: v59.97: brief headline Korean rule at the producer
